Dick Advocaat, 78, is set to become one of the oldest head coaches at the FIFA World Cup, leading Curaçao after an unbeaten CONCACAF qualifying campaign (7-3-0). A disciplined tactician for four decades, Advocaat's resume includes World Cup stints with the Netherlands (1994) and South Korea (2006), alongside major titles such as the UEFA Cup and Super Cup with Zenit, the Scottish Premiership with Rangers, and the Eredivisie with PSV.

Curaçao is likely to adopt a 4-3-3 formation, a setup that allows them to balance defensive solidity with attacking flair. Coach Fred Rutten is expected to emphasize a compact defensive structure, utilizing the strengths of central defenders like Juninho Albertus and Jurensley Martina. The full-backs, Brandley Deeke and Rangelo Room, will be tasked with providing width and supporting the attack. In midfield, the presence of a holding midfielder like Juninho Jansen will be crucial in breaking up opposition play and initiating counter-attacks. Offensively, Curaçao will rely on quick transitions, with wingers Eloy Albertus and Jurensley Jansen providing pace and creativity on the flanks. The central striker, likely Brandley Albertus, will be the focal point of their attack, aiming to capitalize on crosses and through balls.

results.title: South Korea at the 2026 World Cup: Son Heung-min's Last Dance with Hong Myung-bo | Fanorate
highlights:
South Korea 2026 World Cup guide: Hong Myung-bo’s squad, captain Son Heung-min, Lee Kang-in, Kim Min-jae, Group A predictions and the Taeguk Warriors’ knockout hopes.
[...]
South Korea are arguably the second-strongest team in Group A behind hosts Mexico, and reaching the knockout rounds is the clear primary goal. Statistical projections have given them roughly a coin-flip-to-better chance of advancing from the group. With the expanded format and a squad boasting elite European talent, qualification for the Round of 32 is the expectation, with the Round of 16 a realistic ambition. Anything beyond that would echo the spirit of 2002.

Hong Myung-bo’s South Korea typically deploy a flexible 4-2-3-1 or 4-3-3, built on high energy, aggressive pressing and quick transitions. The system is designed to get the ball to Son and Lee Kang-in in dangerous areas, with Hwang Hee-chan stretching play. Defensively, Kim Min-jae anchors a back line that can sit deeper against stronger opposition. Korea are at their best playing on the front foot with intensity and pace.

South Korea are well-placed to finish second in Group A behind Mexico and reach the knockout stage. With elite individual quality and the motivation of Son’s farewell, a Round of 16 appearance is the realistic target, with an outside chance of going further if the draw is kind.
